stops.note: to pour, to melt, combined with com- (together)
to pour together, to mix up, from com- and fundere
stops.meaning: to pour together, to mix up

stops.note: carried into French for confusing or mixing things up
stops.meaning: to confuse or mix things up

stops.note: settled as the English word for confusing or bewildering someone

current_meaning: to confuse or bewilder someone, or to fail to distinguish between things
